title: Equinox Lending POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: Initial POC scoping to define workload characterization for Equinox Lending's conversational lending assistant and batch scoring pipeline. Agreed to capture QPS, concurrency, token distribution, latency SLOs, and run Redwood-hosted vs Dedicated benchmarks over a 4 week pilot.
next_steps: Jordan to share benchmark spreadsheet and example traffic profile (by 2026-07-20)
Equinox to provide sample request logs or synthetic load generator specs (by 2026-07-22)
Schedule Redwood-hosted baseline run and Dedicated capacity estimate call (week of 2026-07-27)
Priya to propose test harness and perf matrix for P95/P99 latency and cost-per-token metrics
action_items: Jordan Kim: send detailed benchmark spreadsheet and example load profile - due 2026-07-20
Mark Li: export 2 weeks of anonymized request logs or provide traffic histogram - due 2026-07-22
Priya Rao: draft POC test plan and load harness steps - due 2026-07-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Mark Li (Head of ML, Equinox), Sara Bennett (Platform Eng), Carlos Mendez (CTO)

Summary: quick run through of Equinox's two primary workloads (live conversational lending assistant + nightly scoring/batch embeddings), define success criteria (latency SLOs, cost targets, accuracy/regression thresholds), and align on benchmarks and POC timeline.

Topics noted earlier: QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, PV vs dedicated deployment options, security requirements (SSO/SAML, KMS), timelines (4 week pilot).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, um this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Priya and Maya from our SE team are here. Quick intro?
[00:08] Mark: yeah hi Mark here, Head of ML at Equinox, we own the lending assistant project and the scoring pipeline, thanks for meeting.
[00:12] Sara: Sara, platform eng, i'll be the one running the infra for the pilot.
[00:17] Carlos: Carlos - CTO, short on time today but wanted to join for the architecture bits.
[00:20] Priya: awesome, thanks. goal for today is scoping out the POC: what success looks like, the traffic model (QPS/concurrency/token mix), and what Redwood needs to run meaningful benchmarks.
[00:30] Jordan: quick product note - we can do hosted API for fast baseline data, and Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation. We'll propose both during the POC.
[00:40] Mark: sounds good. our two main flows - 1) a chat-based assistant used by CS reps and end-users, roughly peak 20 QPS, average concurrency ~40 sessions (concurrent open sessions), input tokens avg ~120, output tokens avg ~80, but there's a long tail - about 5% requests are 800+ tokens. 2) nightly scoring: batch job that embeds ~200k docs, but that's not latency-critical, more throughput/cost focused.
[01:10] Priya: ok that's helpful. can you confirm the 20 QPS is sustained or burst?
[01:14] Mark: it's bursty, typical sustained is 5-8 qps, bursts up to 20 qps for a few minutes during peak. Concurrency spikes to 150 during marketing promos.
[01:25] Maya: got it. so we should model steady-state 8 qps with burst windows to 20 qps and concurrency from 40 up to 150. also need the token distribution hist - can you share a histogram or sample logs? even a synthetic distribution helps.
[01:40] Sara: we can pull anonymized logs, but need to scrub PII. we'll try to export a 2-week sample.
[01:46] Jordan: perfect. our POC success criteria we usually propose: 1) meet your latency SLOs (P95 < 300ms for short prompts, P95 < 800ms for long prompts), 2) cost target below $0.01 per user request (TBD), and 3) no regression in model accuracy beyond 1-2% on your eval set. Does that map to what you expect?
[02:12] Carlos: latency targets look reasonable. Our internal target for interactive flows is P95 < 400ms, but we can be flexible for the pilot if you can show a path to 300ms in production.
[02:24] Priya: great. for the baseline run we'll measure P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also test KV cache effectiveness for multi-turn chat - note sometimes transcriptions call it KV cash in notes, so ignore that.
[02:40] Mark: lol noted. oh and we do care about cold-starts - when a new model is rolled out, we want ramp behavior to be predictable.
[02:48] Priya: we'll capture warm vs cold latency, and also show autoscaling behavior. For the nightly job we'll report throughput in docs/sec and cost per 1M tokens; we can show batching gains with Dedicated versus Hosted.
[03:05] Sara: what about security? we need SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. Also data residency in us-east and eu-west eventually.
[03:16] Jordan: Redwood Private supports VPC/private deployments and KMS/HSM integrations; for the POC we can use hosted with customer-managed keys if needed, and provide audit logs. We'll send our security whitepaper.
[03:32] Mark: competitor check - we've been doing some benchmarks against Anthropic and OpenAI in a previous eval; cost is a big factor.
[03:38] Priya: we'll include comparative cost modeling, though exact performance varies by model family. For fairness we'll run same model version and measure tokenized input/output equivalently.
[03:50] Maya: quick question on tokenization differences - you likely saw different token counts across models; we'll normalize by showing tokens and bytes.
[03:58] Mark: yep do that.
[04:02] Jordan: ok timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) - collect logs and traffic profile. Week 1 - run Redwood-hosted baseline benchmarks (latency P50/P95/P99, throughput), Week 2 - Dedicated capacity estimate and run Dedicated pilot tests (if you sign the reserved capacity NDA), Week 3 - analyze results and cost modeling, Week 4 - wrap up, decision/next steps. total ~4 weeks.
[04:28] Carlos: that timeline works if we can get logs quickly. procurement tends to take 2-3 weeks for contracts but pilot can run on eval credits.
[04:36] Jordan: noted. On benchmarking specifics: we propose two scenarios - interactive (chat): steady 8 qps, bursts to 20 qps, concurrency up to 150, token distribution: 70% short (<200 tokens), 25% medium (200-600), 5% long (600+). Batch: sustained high throughput, model: same model family but with batching/quantized runtime - targets: 1M tokens/hour for nightly window.
[05:05] Priya: measurements we'll capture: P50/P95/P99 latency (ms), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, request queue depth, cost per 1k tokens, and cache hit rate. We'll surface a per-route breakdown.
[05:18] Mark: for the accuracy/regression criteria - we'll provide a small evaluation set (2k prompts) to run before/after; acceptable degradation <= 1.5%.
[05:27] Sara: for the POC harness - do you provide a load generator or should we run our own?
[05:31] Priya: we can provide a reference load harness (k6 + synthetic tokenizer wrapper) and also run hosted jobs from our infra. Ideally we run hosted baseline from Redwood and then let you run the Dedicated test from your environment.
[05:45] Maya: one more thing - for compute sizing, the quick rule of thumb: for chat with avg 200 tokens in/out and 8 qps steady, a single A100-like pod can handle approx 60-80 concurrent small sessions depending on quantization; Dedicated sizing will be more precise after we run sample load.
[06:02] Mark: can you put that in the spreadsheet? rough numbers are fine.
[06:07] Jordan: yes we'll put conservative and optimistic estimates.
[06:10] Carlos: what about model variants and fallbacks - can you automatically route to a cheaper quantized model during high load?
[06:16] Priya: yes - smart routing and model variants are part of the plan: route by latency/cost policy with fallbacks to quantized variants. We'll show cost/quality tradeoffs in the deliverable.
[06:29] Mark: any gotchas on VPC/private for the pilot?
[06:32] Jordan: for Private we need a bit more setup and an enterprise contract; for the POC we'll keep data in hosted with optional customer-managed keys. If you want Private early, we can run an initial audit to estimate onboarding time (usually 4-8 weeks).
[06:46] Sara: ack.
[06:48] Jordan: ok let's capture next steps - Jordan to send benchmark spreadsheet and example traffic profile by 2026-07-20; Mark to provide anonymized logs by 2026-07-22; Priya to provide test plan by 2026-07-24. We'll schedule the first hosted baseline run for week of 2026-07-27.
[07:06] Mark: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:09] Carlos: thanks appreciate the clarity.
[07:12] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the security whitepaper, benchmark sheet, and a calendar invite for the baseline run.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings, some speaker labels may be generic. References: shared doc links - Benchmark spreadsheet (link: drive.redwood.com/equinox-benchmarks), Security whitepaper (link: drive.redwood.com/security-whitepaper), POC test harness repo (link: github.com/redwood/poc-harness).

End of transcript.
questions: What should we use as the primary latency SLO for interactive flows?
Can Equinox provide anonymized logs or a synthetic traffic generator?
Do we run Redwood-hosted baseline first or spin up Dedicated immediately?
